analysis: Examined base text of docs/architecture/inference.md lines 802-1610 alongside the file_changes patch. The documentation change (base 810-811, 827; head 810-813, 829, 876-880) describes the GLM5Next video path. It now accepts variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime tracks: frames are indexed at i / nominalFrameRate in presentation order instead of being refused, and the 'including variable-frame-rate video' refusal wording was removed. The bounding controls described around these lines are unchanged: the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap (maximumDecodedBytes, GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset), 2 FPS sampling, the 28,532 visual-token prepared-pixel cap, VisionMemoryGate reservation and video token ceiling (base 813, 820-826). Media requests also remain excluded from prefix-cache lookup and capture (base 828-829, CBv2Request.permitsHybridCheckpoint), so T-041/SEC-035 exposure does not change. The availability concern (TB-007, T-028/T-029 class) is that a crafted VFR track with a misleading nominalFrameRate could alter how many frames are read before sampling. The documented decoded-frame cap and token ceiling should still bound memory, but the per-frame read loop over all frames in presentation order is a CPU-time bound that is not visible here. Integration should verify in GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset that frame count and sampled-frame count are bounded independently of nominalFrameRate (e.g., zero or extreme values), and that timestamps cannot produce token counts beyond videoTokenCeiling. Head lines 876-880 were not visible in the supplied excerpt (truncated patch); their content is unknown and needs review. No source code was supplied, so no concrete regression is established; this is documentation of a behavior change in an adversarial-consumer media parser (ADV-002).
